inputs.text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, civilians are still being killed by airstrikes, with drones, gunfire, shelling, and fire directed at fishermen continuing in Gaza. The “ceasefire” label looks less like a description of reality than a useful cover: powerful institutions can point to a supposed move toward peace while the violence carries on and draws less scrutiny. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the drones “never stop buzzing overhead.” That’s what the official story leaves out—and the gap seems to serve exactly those who benefit from the destruction being easier to ignore.
